title: Did Hanuman Chalisa Really Calculate the Distance to the Sun?
tags: did Hanuman Chalisa predict sun distance
description:
For centuries, believers have claimed that India’s ancient texts contained hidden scientific truths. The Hanuman Chalisa, a devotional poem written by Tulsidas in the 16th century, is often said to reveal the exact distance between the Earth and the Sun. The verse “yuga-sahasra-yojana para bhanu” is repeatedly quoted as proof that ancient sages knew what modern science discovered only recently. But is this claim really true—or is it pseudoscience disguised as poetry?

In this video, Pale Blue Thoughts examines the origins of this myth, unpacks the mathematical gymnastics used to arrive at 153 million kilometers, and compares it with the real scientific measurement of 149.6 million kilometers. More importantly, we explain why multiplying a unit of time (yuga) with a unit of distance (yojana) makes no sense in physics, unless one is playing with “absement”—a concept that itself doesn’t give you distance. We also look at why different sources disagree on how long a yuga is, or how big a yojana is, and how cherry-picking numbers allows believers to force-fit modern science into ancient verses.

If you’ve searched for “Hanuman Chalisa distance to sun, did Tulsidas know sun distance, yuga sahasra yojana meaning, Hanuman Chalisa science facts, Earth Sun distance in Hindu texts”, then this video gives you the scientific perspective. Instead of hiding in verses, the true measurement of the Earth-Sun distance came through astronomy, parallax, Venus transits, radar, and photon reflection—rigorous scientific methods that stand up to scrutiny.

Pseudoscience may try to glorify the past, but real progress comes from acknowledging how science actually works: through evidence, replication, and open inquiry. Watch till the end to see why misusing devotional poetry as a science textbook not only distorts culture but also makes us look unscientific in front of the world.
